items.title: DNA tests show preliminary matches for around 250 Rasuwa flood victims
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 13 DNA tests have shown preliminary matches between the remains of around 250 people killed in the Rasuwa floods and samples provided by their relatives. Further examinations are underway to confirm their identities and facilitate the handover of the bodies to their families. items.title: Govt introduces procedure to declare missing Bhotekoshi flood victims legally dead
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 12 The government has introduced a new procedure to legally declare people missing in the Bhotekoshi River floods in Rasuwa dead. items.title: Road disruptions leave farmers in Rasuwa struggling to market produce
items.summary: Rasuwa, October 12 Farmers in Amachhodingmo Rural Municipality of Rasuwa district are struggling to market their agricultural produce due to road disruptions caused by the August 26 disaster. Transportation services have been disrupted since the Bhotekoshi flood damaged several bridges and roads, cutting off villages and restricting access to markets. items.title: Flood damage makes journeys longer and costlier in Rasuwa
items.summary: Many settlements across the district have become inaccessible after the August 26 flood damaged roads and bridges. In Amachhodingmo, dwindling relief supplies are adding to residents’ hardship.

items.title: Bhotekoshi flood wasn’t a freak event. It’s the Himalaya doing what it does
items.summary: From the 51,000-year-old Tsergo Ri collapse to the 2015 Langtang landslide, rockfalls are part of the Himalayan ecosystem, and global warming is making them more dangerous.
